 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the claimants aggrieved by the dismissal of the award in MVC No.70/2008 dated 29.12.2011 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil judge and MACT-XIII, Madhugiri.
2. The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.15,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in a road traffic accident that occurred on 15.03.2008 at about 8.45 p.m.

The case of the claimant is that, on 15.03.2008 the deceased as a pillion rider along with one Nagaraju who was riding the bike, he was going from Chitradurga to Davanagere and on that date at about 8.45 p.m.

Smt Jayalakshmi vs H M Mohammed Rasool S/O Ghouse Mohiddin on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58365172/
2 when the motor bike was going near Kalkunte gate a lorry which was going ahead of the motor cyclists stopped without any kind of signal by the driver.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said incident resulted in hitting the lorry and thereby both of them have sustained injuries.

Immediately the deceased was taken to the hospital at Baramasagara Hospital from there he was shifted to Davanagere and then he took NC:
2023:KHC:33346 treatment at Raghavendra Nursing Home, Madhugiri, and he succumbed to the injuries on 13.04.2008.
The owner and the insurer of the lorry are the respondents to the petition.

3. The Court below had dismissed the claim petition, observing that, as per regulation No.23, the driver of the motorcycle moving behind another vehicle shall keep a sufficient distance from that other vehicle to avoid collusion if the vehicle in front should suddenly slow down or stop.

Basing on that the Court come to the conclusion that because of the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle,
the accident had taken place.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that, in a case of death without even looking at any of the evidence, particularly the evidence of PWs 1, 2 and 3 and Exs.P1 to P6, the Court had come to the wrong conclusion that the rider of the vehicle is responsible for the accident.
NC: 2023:KHC:33346 5.
Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that, the Court below basing on the evidence rightly dismissed the claim petition.
It is submitted that, they have failed to implead the owner and the insurer of the vehicle where the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider.
It is submitted that, in fact they have filed an application to implead them, which was opposed by the claimants and the same was dismissed.

In this case, as the Court below has given a finding that the negligence is on the part of the rider of the two wheeler, the insurer and the owner were not parties and as such, the Court below had rightly dismissed the petition.
6. In this case as per the police records the driver of the lorry is at fault and the charge-sheet is also filed against him.

The Court below had given a finding that itself is not sufficient and there should be independent evidence on the part of the claimants and as the safe distance was not maintained by the driver of the vehicle, the accident had taken place and claim petition was NC: 2023:KHC:33346 dismissed.
Considering fact that it is a case of death, the Court below ought not to have dismissed the case with such cryptic findings.

Hence, the order under challenge in this appeal is set aside and the matter is remanded back to the trial court for fresh consideration claimants shall implead the owner as well as the insurer of the bike on which the deceased was traveling.
As the accident of the year 2008, the Tribunal shall disposed of the case as expeditiously as possible, but not later then four months.
7. The parties shall appear before the Court without any further notice on 03.10.2023.
